body_ar: إن الله غني عن عباده، وهم فقراء إليه، وقد أمرهم أن يسألوه ويدعوه، وفتح لهم أبواب رحمته، وعلمهم كيف يدعونه وبما يدعونه، فما على العباد إلا أن يطرقوا أبواب رحمته، ويطلبوه من فضله. مشروعية الدعاء وآدابه: إن الحمد لله، نحمده ونستعينه، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له، ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليما كثيراً. يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا [النساء:1] . يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا * يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا [الأحزاب:70-71] . أما بعد: فإن خير الحديث كتاب الله، وخير الهدي هدي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وشر الأمور محدثاتها، وكل محدثة بدعة، وكل بدعة ضلالة...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God has no need of His servants, and they stand in need of Him. He has commanded them to ask of Him and to call upon Him, has opened to them the doors of His mercy, and has taught them how to call upon Him and with what to call upon Him. So the servants have only to knock at the doors of His mercy and to seek of Him from His bounty.

## The legitimacy of supplication and its proprieties

Praise belongs to God. We praise Him, we seek His help, and we take refuge in God from the evils of our own selves and from the ill of our deeds. Whomever God guides, none can lead astray; and whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger — may God bless him, and his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace.

{O humankind, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate, and from the two of them spread abroad many men and women. Be mindful of God, in whose name you make demands of one another, and of the ties of kinship. Truly God is ever watchful over you.} [al-Nisāʾ 1]

{O you who believe, be mindful of God and speak words that hit the mark: He will set your deeds right for you and forgive you your sins. Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has won a great victory.} [al-Aḥzāb 70–71]

To proceed: the best of speech is the Book of God, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The worst of matters are those newly introduced; every newly introduced matter is an innovation in religion (bidʿah), and every innovation is misguidance...

flags.context: the scriptural verses of the khutbat al-hajah opening, against the same formula in record 666
options: translate the two verses present, mark the gap, and do not restore the missing third
supply the missing third verse from the standard formula
flags.note: IMPORTANT, and it corroborates a finding made in record 666. The standard khutbat al-ḥājah carries three verses — Āl ʿImrān 3:102, al-Nisāʾ 4:1 and al-Aḥzāb 33:70-71. This record, like record 666 in the same slice, has only the second and third; 3:102 is absent from both. That the same verse is missing from the same formula in two independent records, prepared by different hands at different times, indicates a defective house template rather than a slip in one record. Style guide section 11 applies: the lacuna is left visible and the text has NOT been restored. Unlike record 666, this record does separate the two surviving verses and does give references, in its own bracket style, which the English preserves.

flags.note: Record 666 gives this clause without 'every newly introduced matter is an innovation', going straight from 'the worst of matters are those newly introduced' to 'every innovation is misguidance'. This record has the fuller wording. Both are current forms of the formula. Each is rendered as served and neither has been completed from the other.

flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words. Here the transcribed portion is entirely liturgical formula — the sermon opening and its verses — so the record contains no substantive words of the Sheikh's on its announced subject.

options: render as a statement, as the title does, with no attribution added
mark it as a prophetic report and supply the source
flags.note: The title is the wording of a well-known prophetic report, but the record presents it as a title and gives no narrator, collection or grading. Style guide section 4 forbids supplying any; none has been supplied, and the English renders it as the plain statement the title makes it.

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.
The opening is the khutbat al-ḥājah, a fixed recited formula; the Arabic is the operative text and is retained in full in body_ar per style guide section 4.

The Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic. The source's own reference style, sura name and verse number in square brackets, has been kept rather than regularised, because here the source does supply references and the bracket form is its own.
This record and record 666 should be read together by whoever settles the house treatment of the khutbat al-ḥājah.
